items.stem: A site adds a valid web app manifest but no service worker. Which capability does it still LACK?

options.text: Offline access to previously visited pages
options.rationale: Correct: offline support requires a service worker to cache and serve responses.

options.text: An install prompt entry via the manifest
options.rationale: The manifest contributes to installability criteria.

items.explanation: Correct: offline support requires a service worker to cache and serve responses.

items.stem: Which TWO happen during the service worker lifecycle? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The install event is a good place to precache the app shell
options.rationale: Correct: install is used to populate caches.

options.text: The activate event is a good place to delete old caches
options.rationale: Correct: activate commonly cleans up previous cache versions.

options.text: The fetch event fires before install completes
options.rationale: fetch handling applies after activation, for controlled clients.

options.text: A new worker always controls open pages immediately
options.rationale: It waits unless skipWaiting and clients.claim are used.

items.explanation: Correct: install is used to populate caches.

items.stem: Why is cache-first a poor strategy for a frequently updated news feed API?

options.text: It serves stale cached data and may never fetch fresh content
options.rationale: Correct: cache-first prefers the cache, so updates are missed without extra logic.

options.text: It cannot be used over HTTPS
options.rationale: Caching strategies are unrelated to the HTTPS requirement.
Cache reads do not block the main thread.
Caching strategy has no effect on the manifest.
